scientific_question: Among geographically supported Lepidoptera source-target pairs, does similarity in the spatial footprint of larval host resources predict how well post-IBD spatial genetic structure transfers from the source species to the target species?
why_this_is_primary: Larval host resources are an external biological constraint on where Lepidoptera populations can be connected. The predictor was built without sequence identity, pairwise genetic distance, T_st, or an ecology-genetics association, and the frozen design shows broad non-degenerate pairwise variation largely orthogonal to geographic support.

primary_predictor.name: R_host_st
primary_predictor.definition: continuous Jaccard overlap of frozen primary-native larval host-resource WGSrpd3 footprint vectors
primary_predictor.direction: larger overlap predicts larger source-to-target transfer skill
primary_predictor.standardization: z-score over the frozen eligible directed-pair set before response opening

response.name: T_st
response.definition: source-only to target post-IBD transfer skill under the unchanged TTF transfer operator, scored by Spearman association between source-field prediction and target post-IBD edge turnover

predeclared_controls.edge_count_ratio_excluded_from_primary_m: prospectively excluded because its response-blind Spearman correlation with locality_count_ratio is approximately 0.994; locality-count mismatch is retained as the single sampling-size control

primary_estimand.conceptual_model: T_st = alpha_t + gamma_s + beta_R*z(R_host_st) + beta_G*coverage_st + beta_D*log1p(centroid_distance_km_st) + beta_M*abs(log(locality_count_ratio_st)) + beta_F*same_family_st + epsilon_st
primary_estimand.final_inference_family: must preserve both shared-source and shared-target dependence and must pass frozen synthetic Type-I/power qualification before empirical opening

synthetic_qualification.private_null_requirement: Wilson 95% upper rejection bound <= 0.10 in every frozen null cell
synthetic_qualification.relational_power_requirement: Wilson 95% lower rejection bound >= 0.80 at the prospectively frozen minimally meaningful beta_R effect
candidate_inference_families: two-way source/target cluster bootstrap or cluster-robust score test
crossed source-target random-effects model with calibrated one-sided test
restricted source/target-label permutation preserving the frozen pair-support graph
synthetic_qualification.selection_rule: choose only from synthetic Type-I/power and numerical stability; never from empirical genetic response

secondary_only.host_breadth: number of resolved primary-native host species
secondary_only.same_host_identity: descriptive or separately qualified; cannot replace footprint Jaccard
secondary_only.habitat_environment_similarity: cross-taxon external-generalization successor; GBIF feasibility may continue response-blind but does not gate this host-resource primary study

interpretation.positive: Lepidoptera spatial genetic information is more transferable between species that face similar host-resource landscapes, beyond geographic opportunity, broad family membership, source quality, target predictability, and sampling-geometry mismatch.
interpretation.null_with_power: the frozen host-resource footprint relation does not explain source-target transfer heterogeneity in the tested Lepidoptera panel.

prohibited: retune the completed unconditional TTF result
reuse same-order source-pool selection as the primary test
choose a host-overlap threshold from genetic outcomes
replace host-resource Jaccard with habitat similarity after seeing beta_R
drop families or targets because their empirical T_st is unfavorable
treat the response-blind GBIF habitat feasibility study as a rescue analysis
